title: Under the Wave off Kanagawa (Kanagawa oki nami ura), also known as The Great Wave, from the series "Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji (Fugaku sanjūrokkei)"

image.credit: Art Institute of Chicago, Clarence Buckingham Collection

phase.label: Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji, begun at age 70

source.label: Art Institute of Chicago collection description

highlight.text: Several thousand impressions were taken of the design from the cherry-wood printing blocks, literally as many as the publisher could sell.

source.label: The Met: Art of the Pleasure Quarters and the Ukiyo-e Style

work.text: Katsushika Hokusai’s much celebrated series, Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji (Fugaku sanjûrokkei), was begun in 1830, when the artist was 70 years old. This tour-de-force series established the popularity of landscape prints, which continues to this day.

moment.text: Perhaps most striking about the series is Hokusai’s copious use of the newly affordable Berlin blue pigment, featured in many of the compositions in the color for the sky and water.

matters.lead: In the colophon to One Hundred Views of Mount Fuji:
matters.text: At seventy-three years I partly understood the structure of animals, birds, insects and fishes, and the life of grasses and plants.

source.author: Katsushika Hokusai
source.title: Colophon to One Hundred Views of Mount Fuji, quoted in “Hokusai”
